findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied, too-large file). Production unwrap is forbidden.
findings.failure_mode: any unavailable or unreadable audit file crashes the entire process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle.
findings.fix: Return a typed error (e.g. Result<Vec<Record>, AuditError>) and propagate with ? or map_err. Signature: pub fn load_audits(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, AuditError>

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on malformed numeric input. Production unwrap is forbidden.
findings.failure_mode: a single non-numeric field in any audit line aborts the entire batch instead of reporting which record failed and why.
findings.fix: Use checked parse: parts[1].parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError{line_index, source: e}) and return Result<Vec<Record>, AuditError>

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>() as u16 is a lossy as-conversion that silently truncates values above 65535. Forbidden lossy as conversion.
findings.failure_mode: a value of 70000 silently becomes 4471, corrupting audit data with no error or warning.
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) with map_err to convert fallibly, returning a typed overflow error instead of silent truncation.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked indexing into a Vec with no length check. If a line has fewer than 2 comma-separated fields, this panics.
findings.failure_mode: a line with only one field or an empty line triggers an index-out-of-bounds panic, crashing the batch load.
findings.fix: Check parts.len() >= 2 before indexing, or use iterator methods like .get(0) and .get(1) with map_err for typed errors.

findings.problem: println!() performs hidden I/O (stdout) inside a data-parsing function that claims to return Records. I/O must be isolated in the imperative shell.
findings.failure_mode: the parsing core has an observable side effect that cannot be tested in isolation, pollutes stdout during tests, and breaks functional purity.
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing core. If logging is needed, pass an observer/cb trait or log at the shell layer after parsing completes.

findings.problem: load_audits mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic in a single function. I/O must be separated from pure domain logic.
findings.failure_mode: the parsing logic cannot be unit-tested without involving the filesystem, and the function cannot be composed with async I/O or in-memory data sources.
findings.fix: Split into: (1) pub fn parse_audit_lines(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> — pure deterministic core; (2) pub async fn load_audits(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, AuditError> — shell that reads files and delegates to parse_audit_lines.

findings.problem: Record struct uses pub fields with no validation — any code can construct Record with invalid name (empty/whitespace) or value. No type-level invariants.
findings.failure_mode: illegal Record states (empty name, negative value if value were signed) are representable at compile time, pushing validation burden on every consumer.
findings.fix: Add a private constructor: impl Record { pub fn new(name: String, value: u16) -> Option<Self> { if name.is_empty() { None } else { Some(Record { name, value }) } } } and make fields private.

findings.problem: line.split(',') then collect into Vec<String> allocates a full Vec of owned Strings for simple delimited parsing. split_once would be more allocation-efficient for two-field lines.
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocations per line increase memory pressure and GC pressure; for large audit files this is a measurable performance regression.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get (name_part, value_part) without collecting into a Vec, then trim each part individually.

findings.problem: No error type exists. All failures (I/O, parse, index, overflow) collapse into panic. No typed error taxonomy.
findings.failure_mode: consumers cannot distinguish file-not-found from malformed data from overflow, preventing targeted recovery or retry strategies.
findings.fix: Define an enum: pub enum AuditError { Io(io::Error), Parse(ParseError), Overflow { value: String }, MissingField { line: usize } }. Use map_err at each failure point.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_audits throughput or memory usage
no profiler evidence for allocation hot path in the parsing loop
no allocation audit (e.g. cargo-show-asm, alloc-count, or valgrind) for the split+collect pattern
no command-level evidence that this code compiles or passes tests
residual_risk: This crate has 8 blockers and 2 warnings. The most critical risk is silent data corruption via lossy u32->u16 as-conversion combined with multiple panic-on-error paths. A single malformed line in an audit file will crash the process rather than report which record failed. Functional core is entirely absent — I/O and logging are embedded in the parsing function. Without a typed error system, callers have zero recovery options. The code must be split into pure parsing (testable without filesystem) and a shell layer for I/O before any review pass can be considered. No benchmarks, profiler, or allocation evidence exist to validate performance claims.
